The main advance is a sharper formulation of the unresolved problem: one fixed translated probe now detects every possible off-critical zero. The later notes isolate the missing estimate as a signed prime-covariance bound; the local certificates and finite-range sign results do not yet supply that global bound.

The newest notes go beyond the manuscript’s selective-loss summary. They control the negative arithmetic remainder and the outer frequencies, leaving a specific central-frequency estimate open. I’m also checking whether the investigation can aim for a weaker growth bound, since the quadratic target is more precise than the RH implication requires.

The project has made substantial progress in its analytic framework and in isolating the missing arithmetic estimate. **RH and all-window positivity remain unproved.** The strongest advance is that one explicit prepared probe now detects every possible off-critical zero; the latest work narrows its unresolved growth bound to a specific signed central-frequency projection.

I reviewed the requested handoff, the selective-loss overview, the investigation README, the manuscript, and the subsequent notes 08–09 with their reviews.

The progress so far is:

- **A substantial critical-boundary theorem package.** The manuscript establishes uniform trace bounds, critical-zero limits for the positive majorant and fixed Abel regularizations, and localization of possible exact-projection loss. Exact projection mass survival remains open. The rational counterexample shows why local phase concentration and a prelimit gap cannot establish survival. [Main theorem and scope](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/manuscript.tex:235).

- **Exact finite arithmetic identities and useful local positivity.** Finite Euler products now have an exact boundary identity with the compressed inverse metric retained. Full prepared-source comparisons are certified at \(L=1\) and \(L=6/5\). Several stronger proposals have been ruled out: fixed-prime all-support comparison, the mean-only correction sign, and certain finite-rank repairs. These obstructions help prevent repeated investment in unsuccessful routes. [Investigation overview](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/README.md).

- **One fixed probe gives an RH equivalence.** Its signed prime covariance is bounded or subexponential exactly when RH holds; either-sign and weighted-integral criteria also suffice. Higher prime powers contribute a vanishing correction. This substantially simplifies the object to study, while retaining the requirement of unbounded separation. [Single-probe theorem](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/manuscript.tex:2113).

- **Selective loss has a sound construction and controlled diagonal.** The independently positive archimedean reference gives an exact positive-square decomposition. Complete response energy satisfies \(J=D+\Theta\), with unconditional quadratic bounds on \(D\). Certified finite results include \(\Theta<-5\) throughout \([100,225]\), \(|M_g|<1.48\) throughout \([2,500]\), and a seven-source Gram lower bound of \(1/20\). Their scopes remain finite. [Selective-loss results](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/manuscript.tex:2575).

- **Notes 08–09 identify the current frontier.** The singular-series model cancels the diagonal’s leading term. For actual primes, the negative remainder is controlled, four harmless Chebyshev-error trends are removed exactly, and outer frequencies satisfy the target bound. The positive remainder and central signed projection remain open. These developments go beyond the manuscript’s current summary. [Latest continuation](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/notes/selective-loss-program/09_actual_error_projection_and_frequency_20261003.md:23).

For the next investigations, I would prioritize:

1. **The exact central projection in note 09, equation (19).** This is the most focused arithmetic target currently available. Preserve the joint frequency phases and both physical boundary caps. The fitted-error norm is a useful sufficient alternative, but it estimates more than the exact projection requires. The next deliverable should test a proposed unconditional arithmetic input against this precise expression and calculate its resulting exponent and exceptional-shift costs. [Central target](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/notes/selective-loss-program/09_actual_error_projection_and_frequency_20261003.md:296).

2. **Relax the quantitative target to permit subpower losses.** My inference from the existing normalization is that it suffices to prove
   \[
   \int_X^{2X}|V(x)|^2\,dx=O_\delta(X^{2+\delta})
   \qquad\text{for every }\delta>0.
   \]
   This allows more loss than \(X^2\log X\), yet still gives subexponential cumulative energy and forces RH. It remains RH-equivalent when required for every \(\delta\). A bound for one fixed \(0<\delta<1\) would already exclude zeros with \(\Re\rho>1/2+\delta/2\), providing a precise intermediate milestone. [Normalization](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/notes/selective-loss-program/06_global_mechanism_tests_20261003.md:289), [energy abscissa](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/notes/selective-loss-program/07_weighted_energy_abscissa_20261003.md:100).

3. **Pursue independent specialist review in parallel.** The mature operator results, single-probe equivalence, and newest arithmetic reductions warrant external verification and priority assessment. Exact zeta projection-mass survival is also a distinct operator-theoretic investigation with potential value; resolving it would still leave the complete arithmetic identification to address.

The literature checks support the project’s caution: the unconditional singular-series calculation supplies no actual-prime error bound, and the cited mean-square upper theorem assumes RH. [Montgomery–Soundararajan](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0409258), [Brent–Platt–Trudgian](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2008.06140).

I replayed the saved signed-pair and seven-source rational audits successfully. Those checks validate the saved records and algebra; they do not replace specialist proof review. Further finite-range enlargement has lower value until it tests a specific proposed cancellation mechanism.

## My request:
Let's make a folder in the sonin-critical-boundary/notes folder devoted to the second investigation **Allow subpower losses and identify partial milestones. I believe that this seems like a program where systematic improvement is possible. For the first target, I don't fully understand it, but my concern is that we will get lost in a rabbit hole of complicated mathematics without as much to show for it. If we can systematically decrease \delta, that actually could get other mathematicians excited about this project, because it is a real tangible goal. What do you think? **

I’ll create a dedicated folder for the subpower program and give it a clear starting target. I’ll also check what decreasing \(\delta\) would establish, so the milestones are concrete and their difficulty is stated accurately.

A \(\delta\) ledger gives the program a clear measure of progress. There is a significant difficulty at the first step, though: even a global bound with \(\delta=0.99\) would exclude all zeros with real part above \(0.995\), at every height. The current work has no mechanism that guarantees successive reductions.

The first investigation and this one are connected: the central projection is one technical way to prove a \(\delta\) bound. We can organize the program around the exponent and require each calculation to show exactly how it advances that goal.

I found a useful baseline result for the new folder: a stronger published prime-number-theorem bound transfers directly to this variance and improves its decaying factor. It still gives \(\delta=1\).

I’ll record that result separately from the open power-saving milestone, alongside a ledger that distinguishes global exponent proofs, conditional estimates, and finite-range evidence.

Created [notes/subpower-milestones](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/notes/subpower-milestones/README.md), with a program charter, baseline proof, and milestone ledger.

I think decreasing \(\delta\) is a useful organizing goal: each proved improvement has a concrete meaning.

| Proved global \(\delta\) | Zeros excluded |
|---|---|
| \(0.99\) | \(\Re\rho>0.995\) |
| \(0.9\) | \(\Re\rho>0.95\) |
| \(0.5\) | \(\Re\rho>0.75\) |
| Arbitrarily small positive values | RH follows |

**The important qualification is that the first decrease below \(1\) would already be a major theorem.** We currently have no rule that systematically turns one exponent into a smaller one. My earlier recommendation described measurable milestones, rather than an established ladder of attainable improvements.

Your concern about complicated mathematics is reasonable. The central projection is one technical tool for obtaining a \(\delta\) bound. We can organize the investigation around the exponent and require each calculation to identify its resulting saving, assumptions, and remaining obstacle.

The folder’s first unresolved target is therefore **one genuine fixed power saving**. I also documented a stronger unconditional baseline using [Johnston–Yang’s PNT estimate](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.01980); it improves the decaying factor while retaining \(\delta=1\).

A rigorously proved global reduction would give other mathematicians a substantial, clearly stated result to assess. The ledger will keep that distinct from improved constants and finite-range numerical trends.
